policy_prompt_for_memory.description: If the memory carried in holds a value, copy it unchanged. If it is empty (first step, demonstration shown): read the goal instruction and note whether it says 'before' or 'after' the button was pressed. In the demonstration steps find the press frame: the first frame with fingers 0% open and height under 0.05, gripper over the button. A release is a frame where the fingers widen from ~46% to 88% or more while height is under 0.05. For 'before', take the last release earlier than the press frame; for 'after', take the first release later than the press frame (do not take the later put-away release, where the cube ends more than 8 px from any target). The goal cube's [y, x] in that release frame is the placement point. Among the target entries listed in the execution scene at the bottom of this step, write the [y, x] of the one nearest that point. e.g. [86, 100]

edits.modify_from: the goal cube lies within about 6 pixels of target_before_button; from that step on write 'yes'.
edits.modify_to: the goal cube lies within about 6 pixels of goal_target; from that step on write 'yes'.

annotator_prompt.description: The [y, x] of the target the goal instruction names: the one the demonstration placed the goal cube on right before the button press if the goal says 'before', or right after it if the goal says 'after'. Found by reading the whole demonstration. The press frame is the first demonstration frame where the fingers go to 0% open with height under 0.05 and the gripper over the button. A release is a frame where the fingers widen from ~46% to 88% or more with height under 0.05. If the goal says 'before', take the last release earlier than the press frame; if it says 'after', take the first release later than the press frame (a later put-away release, where the cube ends more than 8 px from every target, is ignored). The goal cube's position in that release frame is the placement point; the field holds the [y, x] of the target entry nearest that point as listed in the scene at the start of execution. Written at the first decision step and never changed afterwards. e.g. [86, 100]
